title: Napoleon’s Triumph — map element catalogue
scope: Symbol families and representative crops, not an inventory of every occurrence or a reconstructed map. Interpretations checked against the full annotated rulebook; artwork sources remain recorded separately.
pdf_extraction: pdfimages -f 2 -l 4 -png NTR/static/NTR/rules/NT_Annotated_Rules_v1.4.pdf <prefix>; crops use native image object pixels, not rendered page pixels.
notes: Crops preserve original backgrounds; these are reference assets, not transparent sprites.
Meanings were checked against the full annotated PDF, including its errata. Page references are the printed page numbers (also the 1-based PDF page numbers in this file).
Objective colours are victory categories (§16, p. 24); every colour in a stacked group counts independently. They do not indicate current ownership.

Approach marks are sided. Matching unit-type penalties normally apply only when the defense approach is blocked (p. 16); cavalry obstruction checks the defense side (p. 13), while a declared Guard Attack checks obstruction on the attack side (p. 23).
Capacity is a whole-locale unit limit, not approach width or strength. The road pass-through exception is governed by the erratum on p. 6.
Setup bar count gives the number of units there during setup (user clarification). Heraldic track artwork has no additional rule identified.

The numbered reference map on p. 28 supplies locale labels for later tracing. Locale polygons, approach identities, exact narrow/wide classification, road junctions and every symbol occurrence still require map extraction.

entries.name: Infantry penalty
entries.meaning: If defending pieces block this defense approach and the attack leading units are infantry, subtract one from the initial attack result. The matching penalty is applied once to the total, not once per leading unit. Infantry also has a separate minus-one modifier against a blocked defense approach, independent of these symbols. Ordinary defense from reserve does not trigger the symbol penalty; optional Santon rules are an exception. Artillery-led attacks still apply a matching artillery penalty but do not subtract defense leading-unit strength.
entries.evidence: Rulebook §11 Step 6, p. 16; optional §18, p. 25
entries.variants: Preserve which side of the approach contains the symbol; do not interpret it as an extra movement cost.
entries.association: Approach ID + destination locale ID + position + rotation

entries.name: Obstructed
entries.meaning: If the defense approach is obstructed, cavalry cannot lead an attack, lead a defense or counter-attack; cavalry may still participate without leading or conduct a feint. Separately, a declared Guard Attack is forbidden if the attacker’s own attack approach is obstructed. These two checks use opposite sides of the shared boundary.
entries.evidence: Rulebook §11, p. 13; §15, p. 23; flowchart p. 30
entries.association: Approach ID + destination locale ID + position + rotation

entries.meaning: Pieces may neither cross nor block an impassable approach. Retreats may not cross one either. Preserve every printed occurrence and its side.

entries.name: Locale capacity
entries.meaning: Boxed number: maximum units of a player in the entire locale, excluding commanders; blocks, not strength. No separate approach/reserve capacity. A corps may pass through a locale by road even if the corps exceeds its capacity, provided the locale is not already full and the corps does not end there (erratum). During French setup, a corps may initially be assigned more units than its setup locale can hold only if the subsequent detachments leave capacity limits satisfied. Retreat destinations must obey capacity.
entries.evidence: Rulebook pp. 3–6; §8 erratum, p. 6; §12, p. 21
entries.association: Locale ID + position; preserve printed numeric value

source.coordinate_system: native embedded-image pixels; top-left origin; [left, top, right, bottom)

entries.name: Hill marker and elevation
entries.meaning: Triangle identifies a hill locale; the numeric elevation is cosmetic. Hill status matters: artillery-led attacks may occur from the same approach in consecutive rounds when the attack locale is a hill and the defense locale is not. Optional Santon rules restrict artillery other than the French fixed battery from leading attacks/defenses there. A fixed battery set up in Santon stays in reserve, may lead across any of its three approaches, and approach penalties apply even against its reserve defense.
entries.evidence: Rulebook p. 3; §11 Step 5, p. 15; optional §18, p. 25
entries.variants: Keep the hill flag separate from the printed elevation value and from background elevation shading.
entries.association: Locale ID + position; preserve printed numeric value

entries.name: Objective marker
entries.meaning: Star marking an objective locale. Blue, green, red and black form distinct victory categories; a locale can carry several categories. Objective control requires a corps with at least one infantry and/or artillery unit, plus a road path to a friendly main-road reinforcement entry locale; neither that entry nor any locale on the path may be enemy-occupied. Without French reinforcements, Allies win marginally if they control at least one blue objective and the French control no green, red or black objectives; otherwise the French win. With French reinforcements, French win marginally if they control at least one objective of each green, red and black category and the Allies control no blue objectives; otherwise Allies win. Demoralization takes precedence as a decisive victory.
entries.evidence: Rulebook pp. 3, 24 (§16)
entries.variants: Preserve every colour in a stacked group; do not collapse it to a single objective flag.
entries.association: Locale ID + position + printed colour/rotation; nearby label kept separately

source.coordinate_system: native embedded-image pixels; top-left origin; [left, top, right, bottom)

entries.name: Reinforcement entry marker
entries.meaning: Reinforcement entry locale marker. Blue indicates French; red indicates Allied. Choose an unoccupied-by-enemy entry locale when bringing pieces on; entry uses road movement and commands. A corps enters together via one entry locale and road. French reinforcements may receive two move commands in their entry turn (the first must use a road); Allied reinforcements do not have this double move. French availability is printed on the Time Track; Allied reinforcements in the 1 December scenario are available from its first round.
entries.evidence: Rulebook §10, p. 11; §6 annotation, p. 5; board legend
entries.association: Locale ID + side + entry road(s) + position/rotation. Main-road entry status also matters for objective supply paths (§16, p. 24).

entries.name: Main road
entries.meaning: Main road: red for main roads, brown for local roads. A road move may travel up to three locales using only main roads, or up to two using local roads or a mixture. It must follow connected roads: routes in the same locale can be unconnected. From a starting locale with unconnected roads, a piece may leave by any one of them. Road moves normally start and end in reserve; cavalry may finish blocking an approach crossed by the connected route. Reinforcement entry requires road movement; objective control requires a road path to a friendly main-road entry.
entries.association: Route geometry + road class + connectivity within locales + crossed approaches; sharing a locale does not imply a junction.

entries.name: French printed roster
entries.meaning: Blue French Army display. The Army displays inventory the initial pieces face-up before setup. Symbols identify unit type; their repetition gives strength. The number beside a commander’s name gives the minimum initial corps assignment (the circled number in this board artwork); the maximum is eight. French setup follows Allied organization; Bernadotte and Davout each require at least one unit other than two-strength infantry. These displays are setup references, not pieces deployed on the battlefield.

entries.variants: Commander names and minimum-assignment numbers are semantic data; border colour and heraldic artwork are retained as printed reference graphics.

entries.name: Morale track
entries.meaning: Blue and red markers track French and Allied morale. The board marks initial levels as French 23 and Allied 27; optional balance rules may reduce initial morale. The losing army in an attack loses morale for its strength losses; retreat losses also reduce morale. The final demoralizing loss cannot come from an artillery-led attack. The first French reinforcement adds four morale. At night, recover half of morale losses, rounded down, to a maximum of four. Elite commitment and failed Guard Attacks have additional penalties. Demoralization ends the game immediately.
entries.evidence: Board artwork for initial 23/27; rulebook §13–14, p. 22; §15, p. 23; §16–17, pp. 24–25
entries.association: Board coordinates; text sub-elements need separate extraction later

entries.name: Time track
entries.meaning: A black marker shows the current round/hour; each round contains an Allied turn followed by a French turn. Night prohibits attacks and restores some morale.
